run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T08:02:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy (alert annotation reports current 18.18888888888889) is explained by a failed rollout of the product-catalog Deployment to a non-pullable image. At 08:03:09-08:03:17Z the Deployment product-catalog created a new ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 using image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 and scaled the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) from 1 to 0, killing the old pod. The new pod never starts: image pull returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED and it sits in ImagePullBackOff, so the product-catalog Service (ClusterIP 100.69.9.250:8080) has only notReadyAddresses and no ready backend. From 08:04:57Z the callers' client spans fail with grpc 14 and exact messages such as '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080' (frontend, and checkout with 'dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted'); frontend answers 500 for the product-catalog-dependent routes (/api/products/{productId}, /api/checkout, /api/recommendations) while /api/cart and /api/data keep returning 200/308, and frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans both record HTTP 500 with error=true. frontend-proxy's ERROR span rate moved from 0 to 1.47/s at 08:04:57Z, peaked at 14.63/s at 08:09:57Z and was 7.75/s at 08:17:57Z. A second, much smaller and pre-existing error source is visible from ~07:46Z to ~08:03Z: sporadic frontend-proxy 503s with envoy flag upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} and egress http.status_code 0, which explains why the error rate was already slightly above 0 when the alert started at 08:02:57Z; its cause could not be attributed. frontend-proxy itself is a victim, not the origin: its pod has restartCount 0, no previous instance, and its Deployment is 1/1 ready.

claims.text: frontend-proxy exposes exactly two traced operations in this window: span_name 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and span_name 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); each has both STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET series in traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

Summed over both frontend-proxy operations, the ERROR span rate (rate of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) was 0 until 08:03:57Z, 1.4667/s at 08:04:57Z, peaked at 14.6333/s at 08:09:57Z and was 7.7475/s at 08:17:57Z; the STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate fell from ~25/s to ~6-11/s over the same period. Span counts are not unique request counts.

Increase of ERROR spans over 16 minutes rose from 184.55 (client 'router frontend egress') and 190.88 (server 'ingress') at 08:04:57Z to 4776.96 and 4782.29 at 08:17:57Z, so both the proxy's client egress spans toward frontend and its server ingress spans were erroring.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans carry status tags error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, http.status_code=500 on both operation 'ingress' (e.g. span 61bc624b6f1038d5, 93 ms) and operation 'router frontend egress' (e.g. span efd2cf83a542bd02), i.e. the proxy received and forwarded 500 responses rather than failing on its own connection in this phase.

frontend-proxy access logs at 08:04:50-08:04:53Z show HTTP 500 for 'GET /api/products/<id>', 'POST /api/checkout' and 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=...', while 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/data' and 'GET /api/data/?contextKeys=...' return 200/308 in the same seconds, so the 500s are limited to product-catalog-dependent routes.

frontend's own client span 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080 - Local (0.0.0.0:0)', causing 'GET /api/products/{productId}' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' to return error=true http.status_code=500.
100.69.9.250:8080 is the ClusterIP and service port of the Kubernetes Service product-catalog (selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog, targetPort 8080).

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog has spec.replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 but no ready/available replicas, and its pod template image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 with imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent; every other otel-demo Deployment reports 1/1 ready with ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-* images (frontend-proxy 1/1 with ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy).

Kubernetes events show the rollout: Deployment product-catalog 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-56fbb5f966 from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0' at 08:03:17Z, pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 'Killing/Stopping container product-catalog' at 08:03:17Z, and repeated pull failures for image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0: 'unexpected status from HEAD request to https://quay.io/v2/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid/manifests/1.0.0: 401 UNAUTHORIZED', 'Error: ErrImagePull' at 08:03:13Z and 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' (count 21) on pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk.

Ownership chain: ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 was created 2026-11-15T08:03:09Z and is controlled by Deployment product-catalog with image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0; ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc, also controlled by Deployment product-catalog, carries the previous image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and is scaled to 0 replicas with no ready replicas.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is in phase Pending with container ready=false, waiting reason ImagePullBackOff, restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-15T08:03:25Z; no other otel-demo pod is non-Running.

The Endpoints object product-catalog contains only a notReadyAddresses entry, IP 100.96.4.116 pointing at pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk, for port 8080; no ready address is present, so the Service has no healthy backend.

checkout's own spans show the same dependency failure: 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted"', and the parent 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"6E92ZMYYFZ"'.

recommendation's own ERROR spans on '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 'get_product_list' increase to 290.02 and 584.56 per 10-minute windows at the 08:10:57Z and 08:15:57Z evaluations, i.e. a second caller of product-catalog is also failing on its own spans.

product-catalog's own span volume (trailing 10-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}) was 2826.3 at 08:10:00Z and 0 at 08:15:00Z, consistent with the only product-catalog pod becoming unavailable.

frontend-proxy is not crashed or restarted and is not the origin of the errors: pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-zj87n is Running and ready with restartCount 0, its container has no previous instance, and Deployment frontend-proxy reports 1/1 ready with the usual ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy image.

Not every path through frontend-proxy failed: in the same sampled traces cart operations succeeded (cart 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'HGET', 'HMSET', 'EXPIRE' spans with no error status) and frontend-proxy logged 200 for POST /api/cart during the 500 burst, so the proxy and frontend were still serving non-product-catalog traffic.

A smaller, earlier error phase predates the product-catalog rollout: between 07:46Z and 08:03Z frontend-proxy ingress spans already showed ~1-7 ERROR spans per 16 minutes, and sampled spans from 07:53-08:00Z are http.status_code=503 whose 'router frontend egress' span carries error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the envoy log for those requests reads '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' (e.g. GET /api/recommendations, GET /api/cart).

For one of those 503 traces (trace_id c40d34eb8b99fc60392d0073a27fdb0e) the whole trace contains only load-generator 'user_view_cart'/'GET' spans and frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' spans; no frontend span is present, so the upstream connection ended before a frontend span was recorded (omitted spans remain unknown).

Rejected: that the sustained high frontend-proxy error rate is caused by the earlier 503 upstream-reset phase. Those 503s were roughly 0.004/s before 08:04Z, whereas the sustained ERROR rate is 1.47-14.63/s and its onset at 08:04:57Z coincides with product-catalog losing its only ready pod; the 503 pattern is a separate, much smaller contributor to a rate that was only slightly nonzero when the alert opened.

Rejected: that frontend-proxy is itself the failing component (its own upstream leg broken). Its egress 'router frontend egress' spans return HTTP 500 - the same status frontend itself returned on '/api/products/{productId}' and '/api/checkout' in the same traces - and the proxy pod did not restart, so the failure is reported by its upstream, not generated by the proxy.

Best supported causal chain: Deployment product-catalog was rolled to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 at 08:03Z; the pull fails with 401 UNAUTHORIZED so the new pod stays Pending/ImagePullBackOff and the Service has only a notReady endpoint; connections from frontend, checkout and recommendation to 100.69.9.250:8080 then fail (grpc 14, 'connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080' / 'dial tcp ... connect: operation not permitted'); frontend returns 500 on product-catalog-dependent routes and frontend-proxy's ingress and egress spans record 500, driving the RequestErrorRate alert.

Unresolved second candidate: the pre-08:03Z 503s ('upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}', egress http.status_code 0, no frontend span in the trace) point at the frontend upstream terminating connections before a response started; the cause (frontend-side behaviour versus a network/connection issue) could not be determined from the available evidence.

Correct the product-catalog Deployment's container image back to a pullable one (the previous ReplicaSet used ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) or roll the Deployment back, then confirm pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-* becomes Running/Ready, that Endpoints product-catalog gains ready addresses, and that frontend-proxy ERROR spans on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' return to zero.

gaps: No change-history integration is available in this Run, so who or what changed the product-catalog Deployment to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, and exactly when the manifest was applied (before ReplicaSet creation at 08:03:09Z), could not be verified.

Kubernetes objects were read after the window; they show the current state and cannot prove what the objects looked like at 08:02-08:05Z (the ReplicaSet creation timestamp 08:03:09Z and the pod startTime 08:03:25Z are the only historical anchors).
frontend container logs returned no lines for 08:00-08:18Z (no_data), so frontend-side log text for the 500s and for the earlier upstream resets could not be inspected.
Logs of the terminated product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 are not available (pod deleted), so its state just before 08:03:17Z could not be checked.

The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no data (status no_data), so a policy contribution to 'connect EPERM' on 100.69.9.250:8080 cannot be excluded from the returned evidence; the EPERM error text itself is taken as given and not re-interpreted.
No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was returned by list_prometheus_rules (no_data), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation could not be verified.
Trace and span-metric data are samples/aggregates: span counts are not unique request counts, omitted spans are unknown, and the exact number of affected requests is not established.
Whether the earlier 503 upstream-reset phase has an independent root cause (e.g. a frontend-side condition) is unknown.
next_steps: Roll back or patch Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to a pullable image tag (previous: ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) and confirm the rollout becomes Ready with ready Service endpoints.
Review the change that set image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 on the product-catalog Deployment (change history / gitops pipeline) once a change-history source is available.

Investigate the sporadic frontend-proxy 503s with 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' separately, e.g. by inspecting frontend runtime logs and resources around 07:46-08:03Z.
After product-catalog recovers, confirm frontend-proxy ERROR span rate returns to its pre-08:04Z level and that the RequestErrorRate alert clears.
